lessonPlan.title: Bugs & Butterflies
lessonPlan.weeklyOverview: Toddlers will become little nature explorers as they investigate bugs, butterflies, caterpillars, and other tiny creatures. Through sensory play, movement, art, dramatic play, and hands-on discovery, children will develop curiosity about the natural world while strengthening observation, language, and motor skills.
lessonPlan.objectives:
Explore common insects and bugs.
Observe similarities and differences between insects.
Learn about butterfly life cycles.
Strengthen observation and discovery skills.
Develop fine and gross motor coordination.
Build nature-related vocabulary.
Encourage curiosity and respect for living things.
lessonPlan.weeklyMaterials:
Bug figurines
butterfly models
magnifying glasses
bug catchers
play dough
paint
coffee filters
pipe cleaners
sensory bin materials
leaves
flowers
grass clippings
insect books
butterfly stickers
nature photos
baskets
bug nets
construction paper
crayons.
lessonPlan.vocabularyWords:
Bug
Butterfly
Caterpillar
Cocoon
Wings
Ant
Ladybug
Bee
Nature
Garden
Crawl
Fly
Explore
Insect
Pollinate
lessonPlan.observationOpportunities: Observe curiosity, language development, fine motor skills, nature exploration, scientific thinking, and participation in group activities.
lessonPlan.adaptations: Provide larger bug models, visual supports, sensory alternatives, and opportunities for children to participate at their own comfort level.
lessonPlan.familyConnection: Encourage families to take nature walks and look for bugs, butterflies, and insects outdoors. Invite children to share their discoveries with classmates.

items.title: Bug Discovery Table
items.objective: Practice open-ended exploration skills during Bug Discovery Table.
items.description: Toddlers explore Bug Discovery Table during our Bugs & Butterflies week through open-ended exploration.
items.materials:
Theme toys/figurines
Baskets
Picture cards
items.setup: Prepare a toddler-ready space and materials for Bug Discovery Table.
items.steps:
1. Invite toddlers to explore Bug Discovery Table with hands-on materials related to Bugs & Butterflies.
2. Stay nearby and narrate what children notice using simple theme words.
3. Offer choices and follow each child's interest for a few minutes at a time.
4. Encourage pointing, naming, and short conversations about discoveries.
items.teacherRole: Observe, narrate discoveries, and introduce theme vocabulary without directing every action.
learningGoals: Engage in Bug Discovery Table through toddler-friendly open-ended exploration.
Use theme vocabulary related to Bugs & Butterflies.
Practice social interaction, curiosity, and motor skills during play.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe engagement, theme vocabulary, motor skills, and social interaction.
items.adaptations: Offer larger materials, hand-over-hand support, and a shorter turn. Allow parallel play instead of forced sharing.
items.safetyNotes: Supervise closely, keep materials too large to choke on, and clear walkways for active movement. Check outdoor surfaces before play.

items.title: Crawl Like a Bug
items.objective: Practice music & movement skills during Crawl Like a Bug.
items.description: Toddlers explore Crawl Like a Bug during our Bugs & Butterflies week through music & movement.
items.materials:
Scarves or music
Open movement space
items.setup: Prepare a toddler-ready space and materials for Crawl Like a Bug.
items.steps:
1. Start Crawl Like a Bug with a familiar song, chant, or movement cue.
2. Invite toddlers to move their bodies with the music and theme ideas.
3. Mirror children's movements and add simple vocabulary.
4. Allow sitting dancers and standing movers to participate together.

items.safetyNotes: Supervise closely, keep materials too large to choke on, and clear walkways for active movement. Check outdoor surfaces before play.

items.title: Bug Sorting Investigation
items.objective: Practice fine motor skills during Bug Sorting Investigation.
items.description: Toddlers explore Bug Sorting Investigation during our Bugs & Butterflies week through fine motor.
items.materials:
Play dough or crayons
Small manipulatives
Paper
items.setup: Prepare a toddler-ready space and materials for Bug Sorting Investigation.
items.steps:
1. Offer materials for Bug Sorting Investigation that invite pinching, placing, sticking, or scribbling.
2. Demonstrate one simple action, then invite toddlers to try.
3. Celebrate effort and keep tools large enough for little hands.
4. Support turn-taking when children want the same material.

Practice social interaction, curiosity, and motor skills during play.
